analysis:
The PR adds operator-facing diagnostics only. DoctorRunner.swift adds trafficDiagnostic (lines 9-21) and a 'coordinator traffic' diagnostic at lines 114-117. It runs only when stateFresh, with the daemon process matched and the state file not stale, and it maps ServingReadiness.verdict (defined in ProviderCore, not supplied) to pass/info/fail. StatusCommand+Traffic.swift adds Status.trafficLines, which formats the same verdict. StatusCommand.swift lines 147-150 print those lines only when no lifecycle drain line is set and the state is not stale. A test in DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests exercises the blocked and authorized paths.

No security control is changed. The diff has no network I/O, no authorization or grant logic, no key handling, no cache or encryption code, and no change to what the provider sends to the coordinator. The new output is derived from the local daemon state file via DaemonStateFile.read() and the existing currentProviderAuthorization. It is printed to the local operator's console. The operator already has full local access (TB-003), and the existing 'Authorization:' summary and 'Machine ID' lines already expose similar data, so the only new content is advice.message and the verdict detail string, with no new identifiers.

Relevant threats are T-052 and T-057. T-052 covers mistaking a label for serving permission. The new display does not grant permission: it is read-only and derived from the coordinator-sourced authorization state. If ServingReadiness.verdict were more permissive than the authoritative grant (for example a .authorized verdict for an expired or stale grant), the output could mislead the operator, but that would be a diagnostic-accuracy concern and not a regression in enforcement. Whether verdict honours expiry, connection binding and revocation (T-053) is unverified because ProviderCore is not in the supplied evidence. This is an integration question about display accuracy only.

The test uses sandboxed state and a stubbed coordinator, so it is not a production attack surface.
